The paper presents a numerical investigation of electromagnetic radiation from a charged particle passing through a perfect carpet cloak.
The underlying mechanism of transformation optics stems from the symmetry, or 'form invariance,' of Maxwell's equations under a coordinate transformation.
A charged particle perceives not only the electromagnetic space but also the mechanical space, where Newton's laws dictate.
The field generated from the 2D line charged particle is transverse magnetic (TM) field.
Transition radiation (TR) is excited when the charged particle's velocity is relatively low.
Cherenkov radiation (CR) is excited when the charged particle's velocity is sufficiently high.
The phase velocity of light in the background is c.
The speed of the charged particle in the virtual space increases by a factor of 1 + (τ/κ)^2.
The angle between layers and the horizontal plane in the cloak is 55.2°.
The thickness of air in the cloak is 1 cm.
The thickness of the composite in the cloak is 0.29 cm.
The effective parameter ε in the cloak is 1.26 + 0.0006i.
The cloak is designed to be anisotropic and has a loss.
The spectral component of the current can be simulated by an antenna array with the phase velocity tuned by changing the uniform phase difference between two adjacent dipoles.
The phase velocity of the current is 0.81c.
The scattering field is measured along a semicircle in the far field.
